result:
The proposed answer, t = q − 1, is not correct. Its justification is just an unsupported assertion, so I checked it against a known example instead.

For k = 4 and h = 1, the problem asks for point sets in PG(3,q) with at most t points on any plane and size (t−2)q + t. An ovoid has q² + 1 points, and every plane meets it in at most q + 1 points. Setting t = q + 1 gives (q−1)q + q + 1 = q² + 1, so the ovoid meets the bound exactly.

For general h, the analogous construction comes from an ovoid of PG(3,q^h) with each point replaced by an (h−1)-dimensional subspace over F_q. This gives q^{2h} + 1 subspaces, with at most q^h + 1 in any hyperplane. Putting t = q^h + 1 into the bound gives (q^h − 1)q^h + q^h + 1 = q^{2h} + 1, which matches.

This points to t = q^h + 1, which I recalled and checked against this example rather than proved. In the case h = 1, the proposed value q − 1 would give (q−3)q + q − 1 = q² − 2q − 1 points, which does not match the extremal ovoid case.

VERDICT: REJECT
